title: Max Teaches the Thriller Dance
author: Shellfie original
credit: An original story written for the McKinley Bulldogs.

pages: Every fall, a group of McKinley fourth and fifth graders learns a zombie dance to the song "Thriller." They practice after school on Mondays and Wednesdays, then perform at the Harvest Festival and again at the Halloween Parade. This year, Max is a Thriller crew leader who helps teach the new fourth and fifth graders. Now Max is ready to teach you the moves too. Stand up and find some space around you. Ready?

Move one: the zombie stance. Let your arms hang down and swing a little, like they are made of wet spaghetti. Bend your knees, tilt your head to one side, and make your best sleepy zombie face. Don't smile! Okay, you can smile a little. Hold it for a count of four: one, two, three, four.

Move two: the zombie shuffle. Step to the right with your right foot, then drag your left foot to meet it, slowly, as if your shoe is stuck in mud. Do that four times. Now shuffle back to the left. At the first practice, Max shuffled so hard that one sneaker flew across the MPR. The coach caught it and said, "Nice footwork, Max."

Move three: the claw. Raise both hands up by your shoulders and curl your fingers like claws. Lean forward and reach out on the count of one, pull back on two, reach on three, pull back on four. Now add a shoulder shrug on every beat. Shrug, shrug, shrug, shrug. You are officially a zombie.

Move four: the big finish. Put it all together: four counts of stance, eight counts of shuffle, four counts of claws, and then freeze in your scariest pose. When Max's group did this at the Halloween Parade, the whole blacktop cheered, and even the kindergartners tried the zombie arms. Practice your moves, and maybe one day you will join the Thriller crew too.
